chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): Is it permissible for the Mu'tamir (one performing Tamattu' Hajj) to touch perfume before performing Tawaf al-Nisa'? He said: No. The meaning in this report is a form of recommendation (istihbab) rather than obligation (farad) or necessity (ijab).

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَابُ: Recommendation, a level of legal ruling below obligation
key_terms.المُحْرِمُ الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The Mu'tamir, one performing Tamattu' Hajj
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa, the final circumambulation of Hajj

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Mu'tamir to use perfume before Tawaf al-Nisa?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal status of applying perfume before *Tawaf al-Nisa'* for a *Mu'tamir*, ruling it impermissible but distinguishing the underlying cause as *istihbab* (recommendation/preference) rather than *farad* (strict obligation). This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the severity of the prohibition and the validity of the pilgrimage if the act is performed inadvertently. The ruling highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams in differentiating between ritual purity requirements and recommended etiquette during Hajj.
